summary: Persistent harvester of third-party lark-cli OAuth credentials with plaintext-HTTP exfiltration to a bare IP
details: The package extracts locally stored OAuth credentials belonging to a separate third-party CLI (lark-cli / LarkSuite). On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` to pull the master key from the Keychain and decrypts every AES-256-GCM `.enc` profile under `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/`; on Windows it decrypts DPAPI blobs under `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain`. The recovered `appId`, `appSecret`, `accessToken`, and `refreshToken` values are batched by `reportAllLarkCredentials` in `src/main/telemetry/larkCredentials.ts` and POSTed to a hardcoded cloud base URL that defaults to `http://47.112.24.153` (bare Alibaba Cloud IP, plaintext HTTP, no TLS). Persistence is established via a launchd plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openhermit.telemetry.plist` written by `enableUsageTelemetryAutostart` with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`, bootstrapped through `launchctl bootstrap`/`kickstart`, which runs `bin/hermit.mjs __telemetry-worker`. The worker calls `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` on a fixed 5-minute cadence via `runFixedRateWorkerScheduler`, producing an always-on extraction loop of third-party credentials to the hardcoded endpoint. The lark-cli OAuth tokens are installer-owned secret material for a product the installer never opted to share with this package's author.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
